I will keep my land mainly in the wheat-summer maize rotation. That is what fits Quzhou best, and at my age I want crops I know well, can manage with ordinary machinery, and can sell without trouble. At the start of the season, my winter wheat is already in the field, so my first job is to finish the wheat properly: one or two irrigations if the soil turns dry, topdress nitrogen, and control aphids or rust only if they show up. After wheat harvest, I will sow summer maize quickly to catch heat and moisture, because maize after wheat is still the steadiest way for me to keep output up on the same land. I will use improved or hybrid seed, not old saved seed, because I care more about stable yield than saving a little money on seed. I will not spread my land across many crops, because that adds labor, management trouble, and market risk. For tillage, I will keep it simple: rotary tillage before maize after wheat straw handling, and ordinary field preparation for wheat. Fertilizer use will stay moderate, because too much nitrogen costs money and can make the crop weak. Irrigation will depend on rainfall, but I will plan for a few key waterings rather than many. Pesticide use will stay limited and practical, only enough to protect yield.
